old_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off and leg stump. 16
new_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the oft and leg stump.

old_digest: Although not counted in the over No Balls and Wides are recorded in their proper place on the score sheet. An over should always be finished, unless a wicket fall within two minutes of time (see Law 45), or unless there is a local rule extending the time. It is Umpire’s and not the Scorer’s duty to call over.
new_digest: Although not counted in the over No Balls and Wides should be recorded in their proper place on the score sheet. An over should always be finished, unless a wicket fall within two minutes of time (see. Law 45), or unless there is a local rule extending the time. It is Umpire’s and not the Scorer's duty to call over. 8

old_digest: All runs made from a “No Ball,” otherwise than from the bat, shall be scored “No Balls,” and if no runs be made one run shall be added to that score.
new_digest: All runs made from a “No Bail,” otherwise than from the bat, shall be’scored “No Balls,” and if no runs be made one run shall be added to that score.

old_digest: In 1911 an agreement was arrived at between the Counties that “Trial balls, if both batsmen are at the wickets, be not allowed in First Class Matches.” This arrangement was approved and adopted by the M.C.C.
new_digest: In 1911 an agreement was arrived at between the Counties that “Trial balls, if both batsmen are at the wickets, be not allowed in First Class Matches.’ This arrangement was approved and adopted by the M.C.C.

old_digest: A Batsman shall be held to be “out of his ground,” unless his bat in hand, or some part of his person be grounded within the line of the Popping Crease.
new_digest: A Batsman shall be held to be “out of his ground,” unless his bat in hand, or some part of his person be grounded within the line of the Popping Crease. 9

old_digest: A run is scored:— 1st—So often as the Batsmen, after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed, and made good their ground from end to end. 2nd—For penalties under Laws 16, 34, 41, and allowances under 44.
new_digest: 1st So often as the Batsmen, after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed, and made good their ground from end to end. 2nd For penalties under Laws 16, 34, 41, and allowances under 44.
Where a batsman takes his guard in front of the popping crease and a run is made from that point it is not the custom for the Umpire to call “one short”.
The Striker is Out-

old_digest: Notes on Law 23 If the ball rebounds off the pads or person of the wicket-keeper, without having first touched the bat or hand of the Striker, and the Striker is out of his ground the decision should be “Stumped,” and not “Run Out.” It's sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.
new_digest: Notes on Law 23 If the ball rebounds off the pads or person of the wicket-keeper, without having first touched the bat or hand of the Striker, and the Striker is out of his ground the decision should be “Stumped,” and not “Run Out.” 10 It is sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.

old_digest: A Batsman may be out l b w, although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.
new_digest: A Batsman may be out lbw, although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.

old_digest: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an l b w with a breaking ball.
new_digest: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an lbw with a breaking ball.

old_digest: Or, if the ball be struck or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands “Hit the ball twice.”
new_digest: Or, if the ball be struck or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands;—“Hit the ball twice.” 11

old_digest: Either Batsman is Out-
Either batsman can be “run out” at any time when the ball is in play by any fieldsman, including the bowler.
new_digest: Either batsman can be “run out” at any time when the ball is in play by any fieldsman, including the bowler (except as provided above).

old_digest: It should be noted, especially in League and Saturday Matches, that Umpires are appointed “one for each end” and not one for each side.
new_digest: It should be noted, especially in League and Saturday Matches, that Umpires are appointed “one for each end” and not one for each side. 6

old_digest: A Batsman being run out, that run which was being attempted shall not be scored. The Striker being caught no run shall be scored.
new_digest: The Striker being caught no run shall be scored, batsman being run out, that run which was being attempted shall not be scored.

old_digest: If the Ball, whether struck with the bat or not, lodges in a Batsman’s Clothing, the ball shall become “Dead.”
new_digest: If the Bail, whether struck with the bat or not, lodges in a Batsman’s Clothing, the ball shall become “Dead.”

old_digest: A bowler may run a Batsman out, without having delivered the ball, in anyway authorized by the Laws.
new_digest: A bowler may run a Batsman out, without having delivered the ball, in any way authorized by the Laws.

old_digest: (See also Instructions to Umpires.)
new_digest: (See also Instructions to Umpires.) 14

old_digest: The In-going Batsman should meet the out-coming batsman before he enters the Pavilion.
new_digest: The In-going Batsman should meet the out coming batsman before he enters the Pavilion.

Where there is no play on the first day of a three day match Laws 53 and 54 shall apply as if the match were a two day match, and if in a three day match there is no play on the first two days, Laws 53, 54 and Law 1 ‘ one day matches’ shall apply as if the match were a one day match.

old_digest: The stumps shall be of equal and of sufficient size to prevent the bail from passing through, twenty-seven inches out of the ground.
new_digest: The stumps shall be of equal and of sufficient size to prevent the ball from passing through, twenty-seven inches out of the ground.

old_digest: After the actual commencement of play the ground may be again protected when necessary and shall be protected every night during the continuation of a match, but the covering shall be removed each morning, if fine, at 7 o’clock a.m. The covering must not protect a larger area than 18ft by 12ft at each end, and must not protect more than 3ft 6in in front of the popping crease.
new_digest: After the actual commencement of play the ground may be again protected when necessary and shall be protected every night during the continuation of a match, but the covering shall be removed each morning, if fine, at 7 o’clock a.m The covering must not protect a larger area than 18ft by 12ft at each end, and must not protect more than 3ft 6in in front of the popping crease. 7
